title: Bounded execution of an assignment
statement: Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be resource limits, $P$ a program, and $d$ a call depth. For local-value and memory maps $\mathrm{loc},\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, an index $x$, an expression $e$, a time bound $T$, and a postcondition $Q$, suppose $Q$ holds of the state obtained by updating $\mathrm{loc}$ at $x$ to the value of $e$ in the state $(\mathrm{loc},\mu)$ while leaving memory equal to $\mu$. If $e$ is safe in $(\mathrm{loc},\mu)$ and its cost plus one is at most $T$, then assigning $e$ to $x$ from $(\mathrm{loc},\mu)$ ends within time $T$ in a state satisfying $Q$.
